cards.text: After Ehud dies, the Israelites AGAIN do evil in the sight of the LORD. AGAIN, friend, like hitting snooze on the same alarm. So the LORD sells them into the hand of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigns in Hazor, and his army commander is Sisera.

cards.question: Jabin has harshly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years, and they cry out to the LORD. Jabin has nine hundred chariots of ___.

cards.text: Deborah, a prophetess, is judging Israel, and the Israelites come to her for judgment under the Palm of Deborah. A TREE with her name on it, friend, and I thought my name carved on a handle was fancy.

cards.question: Deborah summons Barak son of Abinoam with a command from the LORD, the God of Israel. What does the LORD tell Barak to do?

answers.text: March to Mount Tabor with ten thousand men
Build an altar at Bethel and wait there
Send a gift of tribute to Jabin in Hazor

cards.question: The LORD even promises to draw Sisera out to the River Kishon and deliver him into Barak's hand. True or false: Barak says he'll go whether Deborah comes along or not.

cards.text: Deborah says, "I will certainly go with you," but she adds that this road will bring Barak no honor. That's a yes with a BUT, friend, and the but is doing all the heavy lifting.

cards.question: Deborah tells Barak the LORD will be selling Sisera into the hand of a ___.

cards.text: So Deborah goes with Barak to Kedesh, and ten thousand men of Zebulun and Naphtali follow him. Meanwhile, Heber the Kenite has pitched his tent near Kedesh, so tuck that name in your apron pocket.

cards.question: Sisera hears that Barak has gone up Mount Tabor. What does Sisera do?

answers.text: Calls out all nine hundred iron chariots
Sends Barak a message asking for peace
Pulls his whole army back to Hazor

cards.text: Then Deborah tells Barak, "Arise, for this is the day that the LORD has delivered Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone before you?"

cards.question: True or false: Barak stays up on Mount Tabor and waits for Sisera to come to him.

cards.text: And in front of Barak, the LORD routs Sisera, his charioteers and his whole army. Nine hundred iron chariots, friend, and they don't matter ONE crumb.

cards.question: With his army falling apart, what does Sisera himself do?

answers.text: Leaves his chariot and runs on foot
Surrenders to Barak on the field
Hides in a cave with his officers

cards.question: Barak chases the army to Harosheth-hagoyim, and not a single man is left. Meanwhile, Sisera runs to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite. Why there?

answers.text: There was peace between Jabin and Heber
Jael was a sister of Sisera's mother
Heber owed Sisera a big favor

cards.text: Jael goes out to greet him: "Come in, my lord. Come in with me. Do not be afraid." So in he goes, and the man with nine hundred iron chariots ends up under a blanket.

cards.question: Sisera asks for a little water because he's thirsty, but Jael opens a container of ___.

cards.text: Sisera tells her to stand at the entrance and say no if anyone asks, "Is there a man here?" But as he lies sleeping from exhaustion, Jael takes a tent peg and a hammer and drives the peg through his temple, and he dies.

cards.question: Barak arrives, still chasing Sisera, and Jael goes out to greet him. What does she tell Barak?

answers.text: She'll show him the man he's seeking
No man came to her tent today

cards.question: Deborah said the LORD would sell Sisera into the hand of a woman. True or false: that woman turns out to be Deborah.
On that day God subdues Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites. Their hand grows stronger and stronger against Jabin until they ___ him.

cards.text: Chapter 4 told the story, and now Deborah and Barak SING it. The song opens with a call to bless the LORD when the princes take the lead and the people volunteer.

cards.question: The song calls, "Listen, O kings! Give ear, O princes!" and promises to sing praise to the ___, the God of Israel.
The song looks back to when the LORD went out from Seir and marched from the land of Edom. What does creation do?

answers.text: The earth trembles and the mountains quake
The rivers dry up and the sun stands still
The sea splits and the wind falls silent

cards.text: The song remembers the hard days: highways deserted and life in the villages over, until Deborah arose, "a mother in Israel." I go by Papa, friend, so I RESPECT that title.

cards.question: So how did it get that bad? What does the song say brought war to Israel's gates?

answers.text: Israel broke a treaty with Edom

cards.text: Deborah's heart is with the volunteers. She tells everyone, from riders on white donkeys to folks on the road, to ponder the voices of the singers at the watering places.

cards.question: True or false: the singers at the watering places recount the mighty deeds of Sisera.

cards.text: Then comes "Awake, awake, O Deborah!" and the people of the LORD come down from Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir and Zebulun. This song does NOT believe in the snooze button, friend.

cards.question: Issachar is there too, rushing into the valley at Barak's heels. But in the clans of Reuben there was great ___.

cards.text: The song asks Reuben why he sat among the sheepfolds, and Gilead, Dan and Asher stay put too. Friend, that's the group chat where everybody reads the message and NOBODY replies.

cards.question: But two tribes get a shout-out. True or false: the song says Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives.
The kings of Canaan fight at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, and they take no plunder of silver. The song says something else fought against Sisera too. What?
True or false: the River Kishon carries Sisera's army to safety.
Horses' hooves thunder, and then the angel of the LORD says to curse Meroz. Why?

answers.text: They didn't come to help the LORD
They bowed down to the Baals

cards.text: The song turns to Jael, "most blessed of tent-dwelling women," who gave Sisera milk when he asked for water. Curds in a magnificent bowl, friend, he got the FANCY dish.
She reaches for the tent peg and the workman's hammer and strikes Sisera. The song says it again and again: at her feet he collapses, he falls, and there he lies dead.

cards.question: Far from the battle, someone peers through the lattice and asks, "Why is his chariot so long in coming?" Who is it?
Her wisest ladies answer, and she keeps telling herself the warriors must be finding and dividing the ___.

cards.text: But we know what happened in that tent, friend. The song closes with a prayer: "So may all Your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest."

cards.question: After all this, the land has rest for ___ years.

findings.problem: Ehud shows up for the first time and the card never says who he is (Israel's previous judge). It only says 'After Ehud dies.'

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: New passage content from Judges 4:7 (the LORD promises to draw Sisera out to the River Kishon and deliver him) is told only inside the choice card's question. No story card tells it, and no card cites 4:7.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: New passage content from Judges 4:16 (Barak chases the army to Harosheth-hagoyim and not a single man is left) is told only inside the choice card's question. The question holds three sentences of new events, and no card cites 4:16.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: New passage content from Judges 4:23 (God subdues Jabin before the Israelites) is told only inside the choice card's question, and no card cites 4:23.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank asks the baker to fill a word of the song's line ('sing praise to the ___, the God of Israel'). That tests wording, not the song's movement or meaning. The wrong answers 'princes' and 'people' also don't fit 'the God of Israel.'

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'So how did it get that bad?' makes Judges 5:8 the cause of the deserted highways and empty villages in 5:6-7. The text doesn't state that connection.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The setup sets up a contrast: Issachar rushes in, 'But' Reuben had great ___. That rules out the positive wrong answers 'courage' and 'rejoicing,' so the baker doesn't have to reason it out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: New passage content from Judges 5:19 (the kings of Canaan fight at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo and take no plunder of silver) is told only inside the choice card's question, and no card cites 5:19.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: New passage content from Judges 5:22 (the horses' hooves thunder) is told only inside the choice card's question, and no card cites 5:22.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: This is a who question, but the wrong answers 'Sisera's wife' and 'Jabin's daughter' aren't real details from anywhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: New passage content from Judges 5:29 (her wisest ladies answer) is told only inside the choice card's question, and no card cites 5:29.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: The card calls the closing lines 'a prayer.' The text gives them as the end of the song ('So may all Your enemies perish, O LORD!') and never calls them a prayer. This matches the 'Naomi asks the LORD to bless them' example the rule rejects.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
